expected_requirements.description: Prior Authorization Form PA-200 submitted at least 5 business days before imaging
6 weeks (42 days) of documented conservative physical therapy with minimum 6 sessions
Physical examination of affected joint within 30 days of MRI request

expected_missing_requirements.reason: Form PA-200 was never submitted. Office staff submitted clinical notes only, believing that was sufficient.
Physical therapy duration was approximately 5.7 weeks (5 sessions), falling short of the required 6 weeks and 6 sessions.

expected_satisfied_requirements.reason: Clinical examination performed on 2024-07-08 (same day as MRI request) — within the 30-day window. Documented ROM, McMurray test, stability testing, and pain assessment.

expected_reasoning: Two of three requirements are not satisfied: (1) The required Prior Authorization Form PA-200 was never submitted — the office submitted clinical notes but not the specific form. (2) Physical therapy was approximately 5.7 weeks with 5 sessions, which falls short of the required 6 weeks and 6 sessions. The clinical examination requirement IS satisfied. The appeal should address the PA-200 omission (potentially an administrative error that can be corrected retroactively) and argue that the PT duration was substantially equivalent to the requirement (5.7 weeks vs 6 weeks, with documented clinical improvement and a positive McMurray test supporting the need for imaging).
expected_legal_references: State Insurance Code §3891.1 — Timely Prior Authorization Review Requirements
